passage: Abstract: "when performing cross-validation, these structures are regularly ignored, resulting in serious underestimation of predictive error."
faulty: 10-fold cross-validation with days assigned to folds uniformly at random; a 5-nearest-neighbour regression on the standardised driver variables predicts the level; RMSE of the pooled held-out predictions, divided by the standard deviation of the level, is the statistic. Claim holds when this ratio <= 0.70.
fixed: Forward-in-time blocked evaluation: 1500 days divided into 10 consecutive blocks; for blocks 3 to 10, the regression is fitted on the days of all earlier blocks only and predicts the block; pooled RMSE divided by the standard deviation of the level in the predicted blocks.
estimand: Faulty: error on days whose neighbouring days were used for fitting. Fixed: error on later days predicted from earlier ones, relative to the spread of the level.
model_family: 5-nearest-neighbour regression on standardised drivers. Chosen by me: the abstract names no model; k-NN is cheap and its error on interpolation is easy to see.
sizes_note: Source sizes: not stated in the abstract (full text not read). 1500 days (about 4 years) x 6 = 9k values; cheap. Dependence on length: not stated.
exploited_structure: Time order: consecutive days are nearly identical in drivers and level, so a held-out day has near twins in the fitting data.

structure_statistic.note_value_source: source states none: the abstract gives no autocorrelation; 0.6 is a proposed typical lag-7 autocorrelation of daily hydro-meteorological drivers

notes: Reserve for ROB17 L3.1. statistic_family other: root-mean-square error relative to the standard deviation (not R-squared, slope, correlation, proportion or mean). Differs from B2B-08 in statistic, sizes and model.
